features.feature: Add 'withdrawn' as a terminal checklist disposition (ChecklistStatus union) alongside pending/in_progress/done
Checklist item gains a decisionRef field naming the authorizing scope-shrinkage decision
Decide the fate of the currently-dead --success flag (documented but never persisted onto the item)
checklist_update refuses a direct status=withdrawn write and redirects to scope_shrinkage_decision_set as sole authorized applier
A legacy checklist item with no status=withdrawn/decisionRef still loads and reads exactly as before
Every one of the ~24 status==='done' consumer sites treats withdrawn as terminal (satisfies 'no longer outstanding') but never as delivered
checklistAllDoneGuard (DEV->REVIEW gate, core/machine.ts:355) advances when every item is done-or-withdrawn
Withdrawn items render as WITHDRAWN, never as DONE, in checklist_get/story_get/session_brief/exports
Withdrawn never increments any delivered/completed/success tally
Scope-shrinkage decision gains a stable decisionId, withdrawnChecklistItemRefs, withdrawnAcceptanceBindingRefs and evidenceRefs
A legacy scope-shrinkage decision without the new fields (B-bf52's own decision.json) keeps loading with safe empty defaults
A confirmed decision naming nothing to withdraw (no checklist/binding/milestone refs) is rejected
Append-only acceptance-binding withdrawal record (bindingDispositions) appended beside frozen acceptanceBindings, readable from DEV and REVIEW without returning to PLAN
The original ProofStoryAcceptanceBinding object is preserved byte-for-byte; withdrawal is never an edit or delete of it
The effective-binding projection excludes withdrawn bindings from acceptance evaluation
proofstory_contract_set remains PLAN-frozen (allowedPhases=['PLAN']) and cannot itself be used to write a withdrawal disposition
The checklist disposition and the binding disposition are two distinct records joined by citing the SAME scope-shrinkage decisionId, with agreement validated in both directions
Withdrawal authority is unforgeable: only a confirmed+userConfirmed scope-shrinkage decision naming the specific item/binding can authorize a withdrawal (a DEV agent cannot self-withdraw)
Per CLAUDE.md handler convention: validate at Zod, at handler entry, and at every consuming gate; test the internal-call path that bypasses Zod

A checklist withdrawn must not silently cancel a binding, and a binding withdrawal must not silently rewrite the checklist (independent partial-withdrawal-per-layer is not itself asserted by any verificationIntent entry)

Minimum-delivery / empty-scope floor: a story must not obtain a formal PASS by withdrawing every core acceptance binding; full withdrawal requires explicit re-approval rather than a silent empty-scope pass
The floor evaluates the effective (non-withdrawn) binding set, not the original bindings, so leaving withdrawn originals present cannot fake surviving scope

Acceptance criterion end-to-end: after scope_shrinkage_decision_set removes CHK-nnn, both checklist_get and proofstory_contract_get show that item and its binding as withdrawn (not delivered), from DEV or REVIEW, without returning to PLAN

Negative smoke: done still means delivered; withdrawn is excluded from delivered/completed counts; withdrawn without a valid decisionRef is refused; a decision not citing the item is refused; mismatched decision ids across the two layers are refused; the original binding survives withdrawal unmodified; withdrawing all core bindings does not yield a pass

scope_shrinkage_decision_set is the pre-existing authorized post-DEV shrinkage writer (allowedPhases PLAN/DEV/REVIEW/TEST); an unconfirmed (userConfirmed != true) decision must be treated as unresolved by any consumer, including the new withdrawal mechanism

Milestone ledger rows already have an analogous third-disposition mechanism ('not_applicable' status + auditable notApplicableDecision {reason, decidedBy, decidedAt}) requiring an independently auditable justification, exactly the same problem class ('legitimately excluded planned item') this story solves at the checklist/binding layer

ProofStoryAcceptanceBinding.verificationTopology.applicability already has a 'not_applicable' mode plus decisionRef, and structural rule 11 already requires 'an independently auditable decision reference' for any acceptance-binding exemption -- an existing mechanism for the same concept CHK-004/CHK-005's new bindingDispositions[] independently reinvents

openQuestions.q: Does CHK-006's 'empty_scope_after_withdrawal' gap unconditionally block DONE, or does it inherit the project's doneGateMode observe/enforce convention that already governs every other diagnostic gap added inside evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence (core/proofstory.ts:1514/1864)? If it inherits that convention, the guarantee decision.json calls 'the single most important guarantee' and 'never silently yield a formal pass' would be advisory-only (non-blocking) under the documented default doneGateMode='observe', which is exactly the silent empty-scope pass the story exists to prevent.
openQuestions.evidence: milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md: '`doneGateMode` resolves via loadConfig(root).proofStory?.doneGateMode ?? 'observe' ... enforce remains strictly opt-in'; milestone-status-done-gate-reconciliation.md: 'the report's blocking is mode === 'enforce' && gaps.length > 0 ... a NON-BLOCKING diagnostic under the default observe mode and only blocks under enforce'. CHK-006's own context places the new floor 'relative to the existing DONE intent-equivalence path in core/proofstory.ts:1514 and 1864' -- the same function these two decision docs describe as observe/enforce-gated for its diagnostic gaps -- but neither CHK-006's context nor its verificationIntent mentions doneGateMode, observe, or enforce at all.
openQuestions.resolution: The empty-scope floor must NOT be a diagnostic gap that inherits doneGateMode. Per milestone-triggered-gate-mode-default-decision.md, doneGateMode stays observe by default and evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence gaps only block under opt-in enforce, so a floor placed only there would be advisory by default — the exact silent pass this story prevents. Resolution: the floor is enforced at WRITE time in the sole applier (scope_shrinkage_decision_set), which HARD-REFUSES applying a binding withdrawal that would empty the effective (non-withdrawn) acceptance-binding set unless an explicit full-withdrawal re-approval field is recorded on the confirmed decision. This is independent of doneGateMode and does not flip that default. The empty_scope_after_withdrawal DONE diagnostic gap remains ONLY as defense-in-depth (visible under observe, blocking under enforce), never the sole line. CHK-006 context and verificationIntent are updated to say the guarantee lives at the write-time refusal, not the DONE gate.

openQuestions.q: B-1909 introduces a THIRD parallel 'legitimately excluded planned item' vocabulary (checklist status='withdrawn'+decisionRef, plus a new ProofStoryContractData.bindingDispositions[] append-only array) alongside two already-shipped analogous mechanisms: (a) MilestoneLedgerItem.notApplicableDecision{reason,decidedBy,decidedAt} for milestone rows, and (b) ProofStoryAcceptanceBinding.verificationTopology.applicability.mode='not_applicable'+decisionRef+reason for acceptance bindings (with structural rule 11/AT_INVALID_NA_DECISION already requiring 'an independently auditable decision reference'). None of understanding.json's facts, decision.json's options, or the checklist context mention or reconcile with either existing mechanism. Is the new checklist/binding disposition model intentionally a separate vocabulary (and if so why not reuse/extend the existing applicability.mode/notApplicableDecision shape), or should CHK-003/CHK-004 be redesigned to route through the already-shipped applicability mechanism on verificationTopology instead of adding a second binding-level disposition array?
openQuestions.evidence: milestone-not-applicable-justification.md: 'Require an auditable notApplicableDecision on every not_applicable milestone row ... reason/decidedBy/decidedAt'; proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md line ~202-206: 'applicability: { mode: required|docs_only|optional|not_applicable, reason?, decisionRef? }' and rule 11: 'not_applicable requires an independently auditable decision reference; a note written inside the topology is not enough' and code AT_INVALID_NA_DECISION. B-1909's understanding.json/decision.json/checklist.json contain zero references to verificationTopology, applicability, or notApplicableDecision.
openQuestions.resolution: The new checklist withdrawn+decisionRef and the append-only ProofStoryContractData.bindingDispositions[] are intentionally a SEPARATE vocabulary, not a reroute through the existing applicability.mode/notApplicableDecision shapes, for three grounded reasons. (1) Freeze/phase reachability: applicability.mode=not_applicable lives inside verificationTopology on ProofStoryAcceptanceBinding, which is only written by proofstory_contract_set (allowedPhases PLAN, command-policy.ts:420). This story's whole purpose is a correction reachable from DEV/REVIEW/TEST without returning to PLAN, so mutating a PLAN-frozen field is exactly what must NOT happen. (2) Semantics differ: not_applicable and MilestoneLedgerItem.notApplicableDecision mean this row never applied to this story, whereas withdrawn means it was planned as a real promise and then review proved it undeliverable so scope legitimately shrank — a post-freeze event, not a PLAN classification. (3) Append-only audit: bindingDispositions is a new record BESIDE the byte-for-byte-preserved original binding; overwriting applicability.mode on the original binding would destroy the frozen promise that F-062 says must remain readable. Alignment we DO adopt: the withdrawal cites an independently-auditable decisionRef exactly as AT_INVALID_NA_DECISION (rule 11) and notApplicableDecision already require, so the auditable-decision-reference pattern is shared even though the disposition vocabulary is distinct. plan.md and decision rationale note this explicitly so the separate vocabulary is a recorded choice, not an oversight.
